tracks.name: Focus & Connection
tracks.blurb: Build a dog who checks in with you, loves your hands, and wants to work.

drill.name: Name Game (response to name)
drill.purpose: The dog snaps its head to you when it hears its name. This is the first 'recall' a puppy learns.
steps: Pre-load 5–8 treats in your hand. Sitting/standing doesn't matter; this isn't obedience.
Wait until the dog is NOT looking at you, then say its name once.
The instant the head flicks toward you, feed.
Repeat & treat.
drill.next: No distractions > gradually add distractions, close and at distance.
drill.tip: Name = 'head check' (look at me and wait for the next instruction), not 'come here'. In agility the name is a redirect.
gear: Treat pouch or a jar by the kitchen
drill.source: Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 5, Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 3, Your notes

bonus.title: See shaping in action
bonus.text: Watch a 12-week puppy learn to back onto an object. Notice exactly when the trainer clicks and how the criteria change.

drill.name: Charging the clicker
drill.purpose: Teach the dog that the click always means a treat is coming.
steps: Have a handful of really good treats cut small.
Click once, then feed. The treat follows the click, not at the same time. Click > treat, click > treat.
Don't point the clicker at the dog like a remote; hold it at your side or behind your back.
Repeat standing, sitting, moving, and in different places.
A few times a day, 6–10 treats each. Done when the dog visibly anticipates the treat at the click.
drill.source: Foundation wk 5, Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Play the Shaping Game
bonus.text: One person leaves the room; the others pick a behaviour (turn on a lamp, sit on the floor). Click only, no words or pointing. You'll find out fast how much timing matters.

drill.name: Hand targeting ('Touch')
drill.purpose: Nose-to-palm touch. A portable focus tool, a distraction from trouble, and the first step toward contact training.
steps: Put a handful of small treats in one hand. In the other, hold one treat between two fingers of an open palm.
Present the open palm so the dog sees/smells the treat.
When the nose touches the palm, say 'Yes' as the dog eats the treat.
Wean the finger treat; present an empty palm and add 'Touch'. When the dog bumps it, reward by presenting the treat on the palm where they touched.
drill.next: Treat between fingers > empty palm with 'Touch'.
drill.tip: Great for redirecting a puppy or getting attention in stressful situations.
gear: Plastic lid as a hand-held target
drill.source: Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 14, Puppy K wk 2, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4, Your notes

bonus.title: Prep a week of treats
bonus.text: Cut cheese, cooked chicken or hot dogs into pea-sized pieces. Bag them in session-sized portions (5–8 per exercise) and freeze.

drill.name: Cookie fingers
drill.purpose: A signal that means 'come to this hand, there's food'. The basis for luring and for many handling moves.
steps: Treat in hand, held at the dog's nose height.
Shake your wrist/hand up and down; the dog follows the hand.
Practise with both hands.
drill.tip: Teaches the dog to watch your body language and value your hand.
gear: Soft treats you can hold between fingers
drill.source: Foundation wk 11, Foundation wk 13, Foundation wk 8, Your notes

bonus.title: Work on your balance
bonus.text: Stand on one foot for 30 seconds while you brush your teeth, then switch. Next, walk heel-to-toe down the hallway. Steady handlers make clearer cues.

drill.name: 'Find' / 'Scatter' (treats on the ground)
drill.purpose: Permission to scavenge for a moment. Gets attention, removes attention from something else, and resets the dog's position.
steps: 'Find'/'Search' = throw one treat. 'Scatter' = throw 4 or more.
Example: release off a contact with 'Okay' then 'Find' (throw forward); next throw a treat behind the board so you can reload the target plate and the dog can re-load into 2on2off.
drill.tip: Match treat value to how high the distractions are.
gear: Rug or yoga mat to scatter on (easier on paws, slows the hunt)
drill.source: Foundation wk 18

bonus.title: Learn your cue words
bonus.text: Pick one word each for 'Yes', 'Good', your release, and 'Here'. Write them on a sticky note for the fridge so everyone in the house uses the same ones.

alternates.name: Push Away and Run
alternates.purpose: Dogs want what they can't have; make that you.
steps: Gently push the dog away on the chest or side.
Run away and call.
When the dog catches up, reward with food, a toy, or lots of play.
gear: Tug toy for when they catch you

alternates.name: Teaching 'Yes' (marker word)
alternates.purpose: 'Yes' means the exercise is over and a reward is coming right now.
steps: Say 'Yes', feed a treat. Repeat until the treats are gone.
alternates.tip: 'Good' is different: it means keep going, you're doing it right (continue the exercise).
alternates.source: Foundation wk 3, Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 3

alternates.name: Informal 'throwaway' cue
alternates.purpose: Protect the value of the name and the formal recall by having a casual word for when success isn't likely or you aren't prepared to reward.
steps: Pick a short fun sound, e.g. high-pitched 'pup pup pup' or a kissing noise.
Use it to engage lightly when the dog may not respond to its name.

tracks.name: Self-Control & Calm
tracks.blurb: Impulse control games: good things come from waiting and choosing well.

drill.name: It's Your Choice (the 'Mugging' game)
drill.purpose: Self-control taught through body language only: the treats are available when the dog stops trying to take them.
steps: Hold several small treats on an open palm in front of the dog.
If the dog grabs, nuzzles, paws or chews: just close your hand into a fist. Don't pull away. Say NOTHING; no verbal correction.
Open again. When the dog doesn't go for the treats, mark 'Yes' and, with your other hand, take one treat off the palm and feed it.
Repeat, rewarding every right choice.
drill.next: Move the open hand around: up, down, to the side.
drill.tip: Timing matters: open/close the hand at the right moment by reading body language.
gear: Somewhere to sit on the floor
drill.source: Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 4, Foundation wk 5, Foundation wk 7, Foundation wk 8, Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4, Your notes

bonus.title: Bake pumpkin oat treats
bonus.text: Mix 1 cup oat flour, ½ cup plain pumpkin purée and 2 tbsp xylitol-free peanut butter. Roll, cut into small squares, bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Cool completely; keep refrigerated.

drill.name: Take it / Get it / OK (permission) & 'This and That'
drill.purpose: The dog waits for permission instead of lunging at dropped things. Builds patience and impulse control.
steps: Drop a kibble and cover it with your hand. Let the dog sniff, but don't lift your hand until they back off.
Then say 'take it' (or 'get it'/'ok') and let them eat it.
Slowly lengthen the wait before the release.
Do the same with toys.
'This and That': alternate 'Leave It' with 'Ready'... 'Get It' so the dog learns the difference between not allowed and allowed.
drill.tip: Class meaning: 'Ready' = get ready, look ahead/focus; 'Get It' = permission to go do it.
drill.source: Foundation wk 4, Foundation wk 6, Foundation wk 8, Your notes

bonus.title: Calm breathing break
bonus.text: Five slow breaths: in for 4, out for 6. Dogs read our body; a calm handler makes calm games easier.

drill.name: Leave it
drill.purpose: Don't touch that: food on the floor, a sock, a toy. A safety skill (e.g. broken glass with food on the kitchen floor), and later used in agility when a toy on the ground is the reward.
steps: Class method: lead the dog to a food container (or toy) to sniff, say 'Leave It' and redirect, then feed a treat from you. Repeat a few times.
Then play 'This and That' (see Take it): 'Ready'... 'Get It' gives permission.
Your method A: drop a kibble far enough away that the dog can't easily get it, say 'leave it', reward with a better treat from you. Slowly decrease the distance.
Your method B (toys): on leash, walk past a good toy (or treat), say 'leave it' and keep walking with gentle leash pressure. Start further away if needed.
drill.next: Increase temptation: open the food container.
drill.source: Foundation wk 8, Your notes

bonus.title: Crate games video
bonus.text: A short video on helping a dog love its crate. Watch how fast the reward follows going in.

drill.name: Crate games ('Your In, Your Out')
drill.purpose: Make the crate a happy, safe place to drive into and wait in. Useful for class, trials, travel, and visiting.
steps: Throw a couple of treats to the back of the crate.
As soon as they're eaten, release the dog by throwing a treat outside the crate (or reward coming out with a quick tug).
drill.next: Build speed in and out. Once the dog drives in fast, add the verbal cue.
drill.source: Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 8

bonus.title: Boundary Games
bonus.text: A free guide from Absolute Dogs with games that test your dog's commitment to a mat or place.

drill.name: Mat work ('Go to bed' / 'Place')
drill.purpose: Going to the mat means lie down and relax until released.
steps: Lure onto the bed/mat while saying 'Go on your bed'. 'Yes' and treat when on it; 'Good' while they stay.
Release BEFORE the pup leaves: show a treat, throw it 2–3 ft away, say 'OK'.
drill.next: Lure into a down on the mat (don't cue 'down'); the mat should come to mean 'lie down'. Feed in position, then hold collar, throw a treat, release quickly before they break.
gear: Bath mat, towel or dog bed
Kong or chew for longer stays
drill.source: Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4, Your notes

bonus.title: Fill and freeze Kongs
bonus.text: Stuff three Kongs with soaked kibble and a smear of plain yogurt or pumpkin, then freeze. Ready-made mat-time for the rest of the week.

alternates.name: Sit & position stays
alternates.purpose: Respond to the first cue and hold the position until released.
steps: Ask 'Sit' once at your side; if needed, lure into position with no extra hand signals.
Don't say 'Stay'/'Wait': the position itself means hold it until released.
Reward often while the dog is in position, then slowly build duration.
Add distance using the It's Your Choice open hand (see its progressions).
alternates.next: Puppy: sit, open hand with treats nearest the pup, one small sideways step. Break = close hand and reset; hold = step back, feed, 'Yes, Good Puppy'.
gear: Small treats in an open hand
alternates.source: Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 7, Foundation wk 8, Puppy K wk 4

alternates.name: Waiting at doors
alternates.purpose: Safety skill: the dog never rushes through an opening door, whichever side you're on.
steps: Practise with the dog in their crate or at any door.
Use the It's Your Choice / crate-game logic: the door opens only while the dog holds position; if the dog moves toward the gap, the door closes, with no words.
Release with your release word, and reward.
gear: Any interior door or the crate door
alternates.source: Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 8, Your notes

tracks.name: Body Awareness
tracks.blurb: Feet, back ends and new surfaces. Confidence and coordination for indoor days.

drill.name: Luring onto objects & new surfaces
drill.purpose: Confidence on different textures and objects; the foundation for perch work and contacts.
steps: Lure the dog across the surface; give lots of treats just for trying.
Then lure front feet onto it ('feet'), and later back feet only.
Increase time on the object: 'Good' = keep going, 'Yes' + reward = done.
drill.next: Lure onto more objects; longer duration.
drill.tip: Make sure the surface is safe for their feet.
drill.source: Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4, Your notes

bonus.title: Work on your balance
bonus.text: Stand on a folded towel on one leg for 20 seconds each side. Feel what your dog feels on a wobbly surface.

drill.name: 'Feet' (front feet on a target)
drill.purpose: Point to something and the dog puts its front feet on it.
steps: Lure front feet onto an object while saying 'feet'.
Fade the lure to a point.
drill.tip: Pair with 'Off' as an active attention game.
drill.source: Your notes

bonus.title: Build a perch
bonus.text: Find a sturdy upside-down tub or bowl. Glue a rubber shelf liner or yoga mat scrap to the top for grip. Test it with your own hand pressure before the dog uses it.

drill.name: Shaping & capturing
drill.purpose: Build behaviours from scratch, with no physical control or corrections, by marking small steps toward a goal.
steps: Capturing: wait for the dog to do the whole behaviour (e.g. sit), mark and reward it, then add a cue once it happens often.
Shaping: mark and reward successive small steps toward the final behaviour.
Novel-object starter: put an object down, stare at it. No words, no luring. Click & feed for looking at it, moving toward it, nose-touching it, a foot on it.
Raise criteria gradually. At each new level reward every time for a handful of reps, then reward randomly, then raise criteria again.
Add the cue only once the final behaviour is reliable; then reward only cued reps.
drill.next: Free interaction with novel objects (look, approach, nose, foot).
drill.tip: Shaping needs good observation and timing; it's the more advanced method.
gear: Pizza box or shallow cardboard box
drill.source: Foundation wk 11, Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 6, Foundation wk 7

bonus.title: Strengthening for agility
bonus.text: Saved link on strengthening skills for agility dogs. Save any exercises that need equipment for later.

drill.name: Perch work: rear-end awareness (pivots)
drill.purpose: Teach the dog it has a back end it can move independently while the front feet stay put, and to move away from handler pressure.
steps: Prerequisite: dog happily stands on novel objects for a few seconds.
Lure (or shape with the clicker) the front two feet onto the perch.
Stand beside the dog, treat at its nose, and step into the dog ('putting pressure on').
When the hind end moves away while front feet stay on: 'Yes'/click and reward.
Start with one step; build to a full circle.
Switch hands/sides and go the other way.
drill.tip: Both directions matter: builds rear-end awareness, muscle tone and balance on both sides.
gear: Upside-down washing tub or sturdy bowl
Squeeze tube of soft food or peanut butter (xylitol-free)
drill.source: Foundation wk 4, Foundation wk 5, Foundation wk 6, Your notes

bonus.title: Lickable treat tube
bonus.text: Blend plain cottage cheese with a spoon of pumpkin and spoon it into a reusable squeeze pouch. Perfect for perch work. Keep it refrigerated.

drill.name: Contact training: 2on2off
drill.purpose: Stop at the bottom of a contact (dogwalk, teeter, A-frame): back feet in the yellow zone, front feet on the ground, until released.
steps: Sit on the ground in front of (later beside) the plank.
Lure the dog onto the plank with a treat at its nose.
Slowly bring your hand to the ground close to the plank so the front paws step down.
Praise and place a treat between the front paws; keep feeding there, with a new treat ready before the mouth is empty.
While the dog eats, move your hand away from the nose and back.
If the dog leaves, stop talking and lure back into position.
After a few treats, when the dog looks at you, say the release word and drop/throw a treat away from the plank.
drill.tip: Introduce the release word from day one.
gear: Sturdy board or the bottom stair as the 'contact'
drill.source: Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 18

bonus.title: Trick ideas
bonus.text: Five tricks every dog should know: Middle, Toes, Retrieve, Tidy Away and Circling. Pick one for next week.

alternates.name: Off
alternates.purpose: Get off the bed, chair, or whatever.
steps: Lure the dog onto something (not too high).
Say 'off' and throw a kibble/treat on the floor.
Repeat; they catch on fast.
alternates.tip: Pairs nicely with 'Feet' as an active attention game.
gear: Low ottoman, cushion or dog bed

alternates.name: Between
alternates.purpose: Go between my legs and sit. A safe spot for small dogs where you can protect them.
steps: Treats in both hands.
Say 'between' and lure the dog toward you, but keep the lure hand going past and behind your leg.
Show the other hand to bring the dog forward through your legs; ask for the sit.
gear: Space to stand with feet apart

tracks.name: Life Skills & Recall
tracks.blurb: Being caught, being handled, settling, letting go, and coming when called (hallway edition).

drill.name: Collar grab
drill.purpose: Make being caught rewarding, so the dog doesn't dodge when you reach for it. It's also the start of the drive/focus games.
steps: Touch/hold the collar, then reward.
Say the dog's name, hold the collar with a bit of pressure, feed, release the collar.
drill.source: Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 4, Foundation wk 6, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Rehearse the vet hold
bonus.text: Practise the collar & body hold motion on a stuffed animal: one arm under the tummy, one under the neck. Smooth hands make the real thing easier.

drill.name: Play & Settle
drill.purpose: Teach a puppy to switch from excited play to calm, and to play with you appropriately (bite control).
steps: Play on your knees (taller = safer from face-biting). Gently push the pup away, wiggle fingers, provoke play.
Before the pup gets too wound up: hand in the collar (and hold the leash so they can't grab it), say 'Settle'.
When they relax, release collar pressure, say 'Yes', feed, and keep praising quietly ('Good boy, nice').
Restart play, then settle again before it escalates. Short spurts.
drill.next: Use it whenever the pup gets over-excited and nips.
drill.tip: No food in your hand while playing; it turns play into wanting the food.
gear: Treats in a pocket, not in your hand
drill.source: Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 2, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Make a tea-towel tug
bonus.text: Knot two old tea towels together into a braid with a handle loop at each end. Instant second toy for 'Out' trades.

drill.name: Tug & 'Out' (toy exchange)
drill.purpose: Teach the dog to play with you, tug, and let go on cue.
steps: Play on your knees (discourages face-biting). Wiggle the toy on the ground; push the pup away a little to make it more exciting.
Tug a few times, then stop and present the second toy while saying 'Out'. Hide the first toy behind your back if needed.
Repeat for a minute or two; stop before the pup tires or loses interest.
If teeth hit hand/clothes: hand in collar to stop (a toneless 'Ouch' or a Play & Settle), then restart. Biting ends the game.
drill.next: Adult dogs: let the dog bring the toy, tug a bit first, then 'Out' and trade for high-value food or another toy.
gear: Two equal tug toys (rolled tea towel works)
Hallway to keep the game contained
drill.source: Foundation wk 8, Puppy K wk 2, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Brisk hallway laps
bonus.text: Walk the hallway at 'late for something' pace for 3 minutes, practising crisp 180° turns. That's the loose-leash rhythm.

drill.name: Loose leash walking
drill.purpose: Walk with a loose 'J' in the leash.
steps: Start somewhere quiet (a hallway is ideal).
Pup on one side; leash in the opposite hand so it hangs in a 'J' from the collar. Treats in the hand nearest the pup (or a pouch on that hip).
Walk briskly, like you're late.
The moment the pup passes your hip, turn 180°, encouraging with 'pup pup pup'.
When they follow, 'Yes' and treat.
At first you may get only a couple of steps before turning; gradually go further.
drill.next: Once successful, move to more distracting places (e.g. back yard).
drill.source: Puppy K wk 1, Puppy K wk 3, Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Whisper training
bonus.text: Saved video on quiet, low-voice cueing.

drill.name: Restrained recall
drill.purpose: Build a fast, excited recall to a specific side.
steps: Helper holds the dog. Step out about 30 ft (food-motivated dogs: show food first).
Without turning your body, look over your right shoulder (show your cheek), say the name, then immediately 'Here'/'Come'.
As you call, drop your right hand by your side and show the toy, so the dog comes to your right side.
On arrival: tug party (or jackpot several treats, excited voice).
Practise both sides.
drill.next: Puppy version: hold pup, handler runs away. Run > call name > 'Here'/'Come'. Look over your shoulder to the side you want.
drill.source: Foundation wk 5, Foundation wk 6, Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Plan your recall rewards
bonus.text: List your dog's top 5 rewards in order. Save the top two for 'Here' only, so the recall cue stays special.

alternates.name: Collar & body hold
alternates.purpose: A secure restraint hold for vet exams and handling; also helps with puppy biting.
steps: One hand runs over the back and under the tummy; the other under the neck and up toward the ear.
Hold the pup securely against your body for just a moment, talking calmly ('Good puppy, well done').
If calm and relaxed: put down, 'Yes', reward. Don't wait for wiggling; if they wiggle, try again and release sooner after they go still.
Optional: a helper rewards while you hold.
Gradually lengthen the hold. Goal: a secure, relaxed 'limp noodle'.
gear: A calm moment (after a walk or meal)
alternates.source: Puppy K wk 2, Puppy K wk 3

alternates.name: Meet & greet a person
alternates.purpose: Stay calm when a new person approaches.
steps: Step 1: Walk the pup toward a seated person who ignores it. At any lunge/jump, collar grab and 'Settle'; when calm, release pressure, 'Good puppy', treat.
Step 2: Pup in sit/stand/down; a person (no dog) walks toward you. If the pup gets excited, hand in collar and 'Settle'; reward calm.
If the pup won't settle: step on the leash and let the pup self-correct, no words; praise and treat the moment they settle.
Visitor takes another step with each success, until they can stand and chat. Later the visitor may offer a treat if the pup stays calm.
gear: A visitor who'll ignore the dog at first

alternates.name: Formal recall: 'Here' / 'Come'
alternates.purpose: Emergency-level cue: come right to me, fast. Possibly lifesaving.
steps: Use ONLY with great rewards.
With multiple dogs: name first (gets that dog's head check), then 'Here'.
Train it with restrained recalls (see next).
gear: Your best rewards, saved for this
alternates.source: Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 5, Puppy K wk 4, Your notes

tracks.name: Agility Foundations
tracks.blurb: Flatwork you can do in a living room: position, sends, and turning away from you.

drill.name: Circle work (shadow handling)
drill.purpose: Build value for the dog's position at your side (the 'reinforcement zone') at any speed.
steps: Walk a circle around an object with the dog on the OUTSIDE. Clockwise = dog on your left.
Loose leash in the right hand; treats in the hand nearest the dog (tie the leash around your waist if feeding is awkward).
Feed constantly for correct position. High rate of reinforcement.
After 5–6 treats, break off and play (little tug games are good stress breaks).
Work both directions. No verbal corrections.
drill.next: Walk, dog on the outside, lots of food.
drill.tip: Be consistent all day: don't let the dog practise crossing your path or flicking away even when walking to/from the car or kennel.
gear: Kitchen chair or laundry basket to circle
Spatula with peanut butter for small dogs
drill.source: Foundation wk 2, Foundation wk 3, Foundation wk 4, Foundation wk 5

bonus.title: Footwork without the dog
bonus.text: Walk the lap-turn pattern alone around a chair: back up, dog-side leg and arm back, wait, then step forward. Do it on both sides until it feels like a dance.

drill.name: Target plate: value & sends
drill.purpose: Teach the dog to look and drive ahead, independently of the handler, so you're free to handle.
steps: Load the plate with food 2–3 ft away.
Collar grab, say 'Ready' (= look ahead).
When the dog flips its head to the plate, release with 'Get It' and race the dog to the plate.
Move the plate further away as drive and speed grow.
drill.next: Collar grab > Ready > head flips to plate > Get It.
gear: Paper plate or plastic lid as target plate
drill.source: Foundation wk 10, Foundation wk 11, Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 14, Foundation wk 18, Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Circle work video
bonus.text: Watch circle work done well. Notice the dog's position at the handler's side on the curve.

drill.name: Flip away (turning away from you)
drill.purpose: The dog reads a turn away from you. It's the foundation for lap turns.
steps: Build on your recall: call with name + cookie fingers.
As the dog reaches your side, lure it away from you so it turns in a 'U' out from your body.
Step forward and feed.
drill.source: Foundation wk 8, Your notes

bonus.title: Backside sends
bonus.text: What a backside send is and how it's taught. Good preview of where wraps lead.

drill.name: Lap turn (cookie fingers)
drill.purpose: Turn the dog 180° away from you. Dogs naturally turn toward the handler, so this builds body awareness, two-sidedness, lead changes and following handling.
steps: Treat at the dog's nose height. Back up shaking cookie fingers so the dog follows your hand.
As the dog reaches you, keep drawing it past your hip, then turn it away by rotating your wrist (left hand = clockwise, right hand = counter-clockwise).
Once it commits to the turn, you both move forward, parallel. Feed.
Start slow; add speed once smooth. Practise both sides.
drill.next: On the flat: back up, turn 180°, move forward and feed.
gear: Cone, upside-down recycling bin or kitchen chair as the 'wing'
drill.source: Foundation wk 10, Foundation wk 11, Foundation wk 12, Foundation wk 13, Foundation wk 13 video, Foundation wk 14, Foundation wk 8

bonus.title: Work on your balance
bonus.text: Practise quick direction changes: three steps forward, pivot, three steps back. Agility handlers need nimble feet too.

drill.name: Wrap (180° around an obstacle from the front)
drill.purpose: The dog drives forward to an obstacle and wraps tightly back around it.
steps: Handler and dog face the same direction.
Send forward with your guiding (dog-side) arm and leg, hand kept low.
Wait for the dog to commit ('lock on'/'hook onto' the obstacle) before moving ahead. Be patient.
When smooth, throw a toy ahead so the dog powers out; tug.
Build send distance to 2–15 ft without going to the obstacle's plane.
gear: Recycling bin, laundry basket or chair as the obstacle
drill.source: Foundation wk 14, Foundation wk 14 video

bonus.title: Make target plates
bonus.text: Cut three plastic lids or paper plates; add a strip of coloured tape so your dog can spot them on any floor.

alternates.name: 'Around' (go around a cone)
alternates.purpose: Send the dog around an object.
steps: Dog at your side. Say 'around' and extend your hand toward the cone.
Lure around it the first few times.
Practise the other side.
Vary the object, where you stand, and the dog's distance from the object.
alternates.tip: Overlaps with the class's lap turn and wrap; see those for handling details.
gear: Upside-down recycling bin, big mixing bowl or cone

alternates.name: Blind cross on the flat (with restrained recall)
alternates.purpose: Handler changes sides in front of the dog; the dog switches sides behind the handler's back.
steps: A helper holds the dog while you move forward.
Treat or toy in each hand, hands pointing down and slightly out at hip height.
Look to the side you want the dog on ('power of the cheek') and call its name. That arm guides until the dog commits to it.
After commitment, turn your head to the opposite side where you want the dog next.
Reward the dog at the hand that's out.
gear: A helper to hold the dog
Treat or toy in each hand

bonusPool.text: Watch a 12-week puppy learn to back onto an object. Notice exactly when the trainer clicks and how the criteria change.

bonusPool.text: One person leaves the room; the others pick a behaviour (turn on a lamp, sit on the floor). Click only, no words or pointing. You'll find out fast how much timing matters.

bonusPool.title: Work on your balance

bonusPool.title: Learn your cue words
bonusPool.text: Pick one word each for 'Yes', 'Good', your release, and 'Here'. Write them on a sticky note for the fridge so everyone in the house uses the same ones.

bonusPool.title: Bake pumpkin oat treats
bonusPool.text: Mix 1 cup oat flour, ½ cup plain pumpkin purée and 2 tbsp xylitol-free peanut butter. Roll, cut into small squares, bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Cool completely; keep refrigerated.

bonusPool.title: Calm breathing break
bonusPool.text: Five slow breaths: in for 4, out for 6. Dogs read our body; a calm handler makes calm games easier.

bonusPool.title: Crate games video
bonusPool.text: A short video on helping a dog love its crate. Watch how fast the reward follows going in.

bonusPool.title: Boundary Games
bonusPool.text: A free guide from Absolute Dogs with games that test your dog's commitment to a mat or place.

bonusPool.title: Fill and freeze Kongs
bonusPool.text: Stuff three Kongs with soaked kibble and a smear of plain yogurt or pumpkin, then freeze. Ready-made mat-time for the rest of the week.

bonusPool.title: Work on your balance
bonusPool.text: Stand on a folded towel on one leg for 20 seconds each side. Feel what your dog feels on a wobbly surface.

bonusPool.title: Build a perch
bonusPool.text: Find a sturdy upside-down tub or bowl. Glue a rubber shelf liner or yoga mat scrap to the top for grip. Test it with your own hand pressure before the dog uses it.

bonusPool.title: Strengthening for agility
bonusPool.text: Saved link on strengthening skills for agility dogs. Save any exercises that need equipment for later.

bonusPool.title: Lickable treat tube
bonusPool.text: Blend plain cottage cheese with a spoon of pumpkin and spoon it into a reusable squeeze pouch. Perfect for perch work. Keep it refrigerated.

bonusPool.title: Trick ideas
bonusPool.text: Five tricks every dog should know: Middle, Toes, Retrieve, Tidy Away and Circling. Pick one for next week.

bonusPool.title: Rehearse the vet hold
bonusPool.text: Practise the collar & body hold motion on a stuffed animal: one arm under the tummy, one under the neck. Smooth hands make the real thing easier.

bonusPool.title: Make a tea-towel tug
bonusPool.text: Knot two old tea towels together into a braid with a handle loop at each end. Instant second toy for 'Out' trades.

bonusPool.title: Brisk hallway laps
bonusPool.text: Walk the hallway at 'late for something' pace for 3 minutes, practising crisp 180° turns. That's the loose-leash rhythm.

bonusPool.title: Whisper training
bonusPool.text: Saved video on quiet, low-voice cueing.

bonusPool.title: Plan your recall rewards
bonusPool.text: List your dog's top 5 rewards in order. Save the top two for 'Here' only, so the recall cue stays special.

bonusPool.title: Footwork without the dog
bonusPool.text: Walk the lap-turn pattern alone around a chair: back up, dog-side leg and arm back, wait, then step forward. Do it on both sides until it feels like a dance.

bonusPool.title: Circle work video
bonusPool.text: Watch circle work done well. Notice the dog's position at the handler's side on the curve.

bonusPool.title: Backside sends
bonusPool.text: What a backside send is and how it's taught. Good preview of where wraps lead.

bonusPool.title: Work on your balance
bonusPool.text: Practise quick direction changes: three steps forward, pivot, three steps back. Agility handlers need nimble feet too.

bonusPool.title: Make target plates
bonusPool.text: Cut three plastic lids or paper plates; add a strip of coloured tape so your dog can spot them on any floor.

bonusPool.title: Snuffle towel
bonusPool.text: Lay an old bath towel flat, sprinkle kibble, and roll it up loosely. Tie a loose knot. Ready for a calm sniffing break.

bonusPool.title: Stretch with your dog nearby
bonusPool.text: Five minutes of gentle stretching: calves, hips, shoulders. Handlers who bend and turn a lot need loose hips too.
